ctx.x: I wasn't old enough to get in. So, that's the first live, live I remember hearing.
Then, they had a Masonic Temple in Birmingham. By that time, I think I was old enough then. Remember Jo Jones?

items.q: INTERVIEWEE: Of course not, because when you look up and see Erskine, Erskine would be on trumpet and I would be on trumpet.

ctx.x: It came through Omaha in the thirties. Speaking about Roy Eldridge, when I saw Mr. Roy Eldridge - incidentally, he started on drums and I started on trumpet. I came out with the then Erskine Hawkins. Erskine Hawkins didn't go where I went; he went to Dozier Park.
Did you ever play with Erskine Hawkins' band?

items.q: Did you ever play with Erskine Hawkins' band? Of course not... I quickly gave that up! But when I made the most fatal

ctx.x: Did you ever play with Erskine Hawkins' band?

Of course not, because when you look up and see Erskine, Erskine would be on trumpet and I would be on trumpet. Until 1930 I was playing the second part to 'Beau Koo Jack.' Of course I had to put a Coca-Cola bottle... 'Beau Koo Jack' in the key of B flat. Mr. Don Redman (HUMS) - that's on the second page and you paid 50¢ for that stack. That was a big stack. 'Beau Koo Jack' and 'Louisiana Bobo.' See I played all those things... But my embouchure went away because at the same time I had met a fellow by the name of…
